answer: Nectar condenses only inside one forge and leaves through a single inlet. The inlet records the heat of that forge for the epoch, so a second key presenting the same nectar is pouring from a fire it does not own. An operator who copies one session into n keys still tends one forge. Those copies share one inlet, and the batch that fits through it is paid once. Holding many keys idle does not draw more nectar, because a cold forge yields nothing and the inlet refuses a pour that was not cooked on the heat of that same forge.
